clue.text: Recognise current learning

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for alternating current
learning in the sense of what one knows, knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges a bit of up-to-date scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise something, such as a person's help, is to admit it openly; a synonym.

clue.text: Penetrate one's skin

parts.note: to cut is to pierce or penetrate
one is I, and the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone pierces their own skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical Latin term for the dermis, the true skin; a technical synonym.

clue.text: Now rich development becomes a cathedral city

indicators.note: development suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Newly prosperous after building work, a town gains city status.
explanation.walkthrough: NORWICH is a cathedral city in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in eastern England has a Norman cathedral; an example.

clue.text: Animal finds deep cavity at last

indicators.note: last places the word at at the end of the piece

parts.note: the womb is a deep cavity in the body

explanation.surface: A creature discovers a deep hole at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian burrowing marsupial is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Tennis that is played by a Nobel prizewinner

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are put into play and moved around

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A game of tennis enjoyed by a Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics; an example.

clue.text: Sharing out the relish

indicators.note: out, as in sharing out, signals the letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands round the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration or accompaniment added to food, like a relish; a near synonym.

clue.text: Drill for attacking an old-fashioned person?

definitions.meaning: military drill on a parade ground
beating up someone conventional, a square in slang

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' marching practice on a parade square; read literally, it is battering a fuddy-duddy, which slang calls a square.

clue.text: He goes to the right in endless ridiculous speech

indicators.note: in means the run of pieces is placed inside the other
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich, as in that's rich, means absurd or ridiculous
taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man moves rightward in a long, absurd address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RICH to RIC; 'in' puts HE, TO and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speech, or speech itself as oratory; a synonym.

clue.text: It is wonderful as a rule

definitions.text: It is wonderful as a rule

parts.words: It is wonderful as a rule
parts.note: rule here means a monarch's period on the throne, not a general habit, and the period is splendid

explanation.surface: Something usually turns out marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually', but it means as a period of royal rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A splendid period on the throne, a magnificent sovereign's time in power.

clue.text: Question a sailor about somewhere in the Persian Gulf

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: Someone quizzes a seaman about a place in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The emirate occupies a peninsula on the Persian Gulf coast of Arabia; a geographical description.

clue.text: No charm displayed by a leading lady who is regal

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are set out afresh, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leading part of the word lady is its first letter

explanation.surface: A leading actress shows no charm at all, despite being queenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges NO CHARM and A into MONARCHA; 'leading' takes L, the first letter of 'lady', to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regal befits a king or queen, a ruler of a realm; a synonym.

clue.text: Attacker of rabid alsatians

indicators.note: rabid means crazed and frenzied, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Who attacks you? A pack of mad German shepherd dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assails, or launches an assault on, another is an attacker; a synonym.

clue.text: In no uncertain terms offers cover

indicators.note: In signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone states clearly that they will provide protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside 'uncertain terms'; 'offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting soil over a body, so it is a kind of covering; a synonym.

clue.text: Coarse youth leader is behind the ground

indicators.note: is behind means the youth's piece comes after the ground's piece

parts.note: the ground beneath us is the earth

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rough youth-club leader lags behind on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude or vulgar, so coarse is a synonym.

clue.text: Go off with a politician going round

parts.note: to rot is to decay or go off
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative leaves while doing the rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory motion is spinning about an axis; a synonym.

clue.text: Hello, turned out to be hotter up to now

parts.note: hi is an informal hello

indicators.note: turned out to be suggests the word hotter is turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone greets you and remarks that it has proved hotter than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out to be' rearranges HOTTER into THERTO, after HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Until this point in time; a synonymous adverb.

clue.text: Plant caught in a gale blowing outside

indicators.note: blowing outside suggests letters scattered by the wind into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant is trapped in a storm raging outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing outside' rearranges C, IN and A GALE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic herb whose candied stems decorate cakes; an example of a plant.

clue.text: Against container designed to destroy armoured vehicles

parts.note: anti means opposed to, against
a tank is a large container for liquid or gas

explanation.surface: A weapon described: it opposes containers and is made to wreck armoured transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitank weapons such as guns or mines are made to knock out armoured fighting vehicles; a description.

clue.text: Spoilt a new design on a ship

indicators.note: a new design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A badly made new layout on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one on a mast, found aboard sailing vessels; a description.

clue.text: Summary is not quite exact

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: precise means exact

explanation.surface: A summary is never entirely accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last letter, E, from PRECISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short abstract of a text's main points; a synonym.

clue.text: Physicist not confused with right information going round

indicators.note: going round means the pieces enclose the jumbled word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: confused means the word not is muddled up

explanation.surface: A scientist muddled about the correct details being passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes ONT from NOT; R and GEN go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895; an example of a physicist.

clue.text: Ask the umpire to demand another judgement from a higher court

definitions.meaning: in cricket a fielder asks the umpire to give a batter out

definitions.text: demand another judgement from a higher court
definitions.meaning: to seek a review of a verdict by a superior court

explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer's shout of howzat to the official; also a legal request for a superior bench to review a verdict.

clue.text: Angry, explosive and put out

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: out suggests the word put is knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone cross, volatile and annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT into TUP, after HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up, agitated or upset, close to angry; an informal idiom.

clue.text: Was thoughtful when it entailed a high charge

parts.note: ex means former, what once was
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Someone grew reflective about a charge that proved costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' gives EX as in an ex-husband, one who was.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that costs a lot of money is costly; the definition describes the price.

clue.text: Is about to contend with climbing plants

indicators.note: about means the word is goes round the other piece

parts.note: to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: Something is about to struggle against creepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is an evergreen climber that clings to walls; plural examples.

clue.text: Four go in to tell the story

indicators.note: go in means the four's letters are placed inside the telling

parts.note: to tell a tale is to narrate it
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people gather to relate the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: IV goes inside NARRATE, between T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, a tale; a synonym.

clue.text: Existing state of the ground

definitions.meaning: in being, as in a ... concern
in horse racing, the condition of the turf, such as good or soft

explanation.definitionFit: Existing matches a going concern, still operating; the racing term describes the track's condition, soft or firm.

clue.text: Virtue that has not been spotted?

definitions.text: Virtue that has not been spotted?

parts.words: Virtue that has not been spotted?
parts.note: spotted here means stained with spots of dirt, not noticed; the virtue is being free from dirt

explanation.surface: A good quality nobody has ever noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says this quality is next to godliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spotless is the state of having no dirt or stains, a proverbial virtue.
